F1: The AND requires OWNER membership, rejecting team admins who are neither organizers nor attendees.
F2: Raw guest comparisons allow case variants and plus-addresses to bypass the blacklist.
F3: Calendar failure results are discarded after attendees are persisted, so failed updates still report success.
F4: Email preparation failures are caught without their cause and discarded while the handler reports success.
F5: Neither validation nor insertion deduplicates requested guests, allowing duplicate attendee rows and emails.
F6: Passing raw guests misclassifies existing attendees as new whenever the request also adds someone new.
F7: Add-guests emails are sent unconditionally without respecting event-type email-disable metadata.
F8: The handler adds attendees and sends confirmation emails without checking booking status or time.
F9: Authenticated attendees can trigger arbitrary-address email sends without guest-count limits or mutation rate limiting.
F10: The permission translation key is absent, so the dialog displays the raw key.
F11: Both new templates pass a translation key that reaches the HTML title untranslated.
F12: The organizer email uses APP_NAME instead of the configured EMAIL_FROM_NAME.
F13: Validation errors survive successful submission and dismissal, and the nonempty error string makes the fallback unreachable.
F14: The hardcoded tooltip remains English when the component is displayed in another locale.
